title: Tiered IAM (Strata) and SIEM Bridge Checklist
summary: Practical checklist and reference for implementing a tiered ("strata") IAM model across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, with SIEM export mapping, evidence automation steps, and example policy snippets. Focused on making audit evidence deterministic and SIEM ingestion compact while preserving tenant isolation.
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic 'strata' approach to IAM (role tiers across infra layers), plus an opinionated SIEM-export schema and an evidence-automation checklist for security reviews and audits. It is intended to be actionable for eng/security owners who must implement RBAC v2, set up export contracts with SIEM teams, and automate evidence collection for compliance programs.

Scope:
- Applies to all runtime environments: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), Private (VPC/on-prem).
- Covers: role definitions, least-privilege policy templates, environment-specific deviations, audit log field schema for SIEM, and automation recipes for evidence packaging.

High-level "Strata" (role tiers) - quick reference:
- Stratum 0: System Platform Operators (core infra, network, hypervisor-level ops)
  - Full control over provisioning, cluster-level config, and grid scheduling. No tenant data access by default.
- Stratum 1: Redwood SRE / Serving Runtime Engineers
  - Manage runtime, autoscaling, kernel selection, and model routing policies. Can see anonymized tenant metrics but must not access raw request payloads without escalation.
- Stratum 2: Tenant Administrators / Customer-Scoped Admins
  - Admin for a specific tenant: manage models, rollout policies, API keys scoped to that tenant. No cross-tenant visibility.
- Stratum 3: Application Developers / ML Engineers
  - Deploy prompts, manage model versions within tenant. No infra-level privileges.
- Stratum 4: Observability & Audit-Only Roles (readonly)
  - Read-only access to metrics, dashboards, and sanitized traces.
- Stratum 5: Integrations / Service Principals (machine identities)
  - Scoped tokens for autoscaling, monitoring, CI/CD. Credentials short-lived and rotated.

Environment deviations (short):
- Hosted: Redwood-managed control plane. Stratum 0/1 are Redwood employees. Tenant Admins are customers and have strict tenant-scoped API keys. SIEM export must include tenant_id in every log.
- Dedicated: Dedicated pool for a customer. Stratum 1 may include both Redwood and customer SREs; require explicit privilege scoping for host-level actions. SIEM export supports both centralized Redwood SIEM or customer SIEM forwarder — include "export_mode" tag.
- Private: Customer-managed control plane. Redwood-run ops limited; deliver the export contract (schema + TLS endpoint) and evidence automation scripts that run in-customer environment.

Policy template examples (opinionated, minimize privileges):
- Tenant-scoped read-only role (pseudo-JSON policy):
  {
    "Version": "2023-09-01",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": ["redwood:ListModels", "redwood:GetModelMetadata", "redwood:ListDeployments"],
        "Resource": "arn:redwood:tenant:${tenant_id}:*"
      },
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": ["redwood:GetUsageMetrics"],
        "Resource": "arn:redwood:tenant:${tenant_id}:metrics/*"
      }
    ]
  }

- Minimal SRE runtime patch role (scoped to pools, no data read):
  {
    "Version": "2023-09-01",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": ["redwood:DrainNode","redwood:UpdatePoolConfig"],
        "Resource": "arn:redwood:pool:${pool_id}"
      },
      {
        "Effect": "Deny",
        "Action": ["redwood:ReadRequestPayload","redwood:ExportRequestBody"],
        "Resource": "arn:redwood:tenant:*"
      }
    ]
  }

Design rules and guardrails:
- Default deny: every new action must be explicitly allowed in a policy.
- Data access requires separate entitlement and an auditable activation flow (temporary elevation with reason / approver).
- Service principals must use short-lived credentials (<= 1 hour) and mTLS where possible.
- Break-glass: single-use emergency key tied to Slack/Email alerting and automatic token revocation after 30 minutes; every break-glass event creates a ticket in Jira.

Audit log & SIEM export schema (opinionated compact JSON line per event):
Fields (must be present for every event):
- schema_version: "redwood.audit.v1"
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- env: hosted | dedicated | private
- tenant_id: string | null (null for control-plane only events)
- actor_id: user:<id> | svc:<id> | role:<id>
- actor_role: stratum-[0..5]
- action: canonical action name (e.g., "model.deploy", "pool.update", "auth.token.create")
- resource: canonical resource ARN (e.g., arn:redwood:tenant:123:model:abc)
 - outcome: success | failure | partial
- request_id: uuid
- latency_ms: integer (if applicable)
- bytes_in, bytes_out: integers when applicable
- outcome_reason: short string (for failures)
- audit_flags: list (e.g., ["privilege-elev", "break-glass"])
- trace_id: optional, for correlation with tracing backend
- telemetry: compact map encoded as base64 or compact JSON (examples below)

Telemetry keys we recommend including (compact):
- model_id, model_version, sequence_len, tokens_generated, kv_cache_hit (0|1), quant_profile
- fallback_model_id (if fallback happened), routed_region

Example event (single-line JSON):
{"schema_version":"redwood.audit.v1","timestamp":"2026-02-10T16:41:12Z","env":"hosted","tenant_id":"t-8423","actor_id":"user:ajones","actor_role":"stratum-2","action":"model.deploy","resource":"arn:redwood:tenant:t-8423:model:m-3","outcome":"success","request_id":"9b6f4d2a-...","latency_ms":312,"telemetry":{"model_version":"v2.1","sequence_len":64}}

SIEM export/transport guidance:
- Preferred format: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) compressed with gzip for bulk exports.
- For streaming, use a secure TLS connection with mutual auth to the SIEM endpoint; export messages as framed JSON.
- Add an envelope header with source_id and batch_id to assist de-duplication.
- Include a rolling export checkpoint (watermark) every batch with latest timestamp and batch_size so replays are detectable.

Evidence automation checklist (packaging for audits):
1) Define Evidence Requirements: map audit control to log queries and artifacts (e.g., RBAC: show role->policy files and audit entries for role grants).
2) Playbook codification: turn queries into scripted jobs (sql/ELK/KQL) that produce deterministic NDJSON output with header metadata (audit_run_id, run_timestamp, owner).
3) Snapshot policies: collect current policy files (policy repo tag) and calculate sha256 for each. Include the repo commit ID.
4) Log extraction window: pull logs for a deterministic window around events (e.g., grant events + 24h).
5) Evidence bundle: package logs, policy snapshot, config diffs, and a short findings.md. Zip with signed manifest (GPG) and upload to secure evidence bucket.
6) Retention/TTL: ensure evidence retention meets compliance (e.g., 7 years for some controls) — automation should tag bundles with retention policies for lifecycle.

Quick automation examples (pseudo-commands):
- Extract RBAC grants in ELK: curl -XPOST "https://elk/_search" -d '{"query":{"term":{"action":"rbac.grant"}},"sort":[{"@timestamp":"asc"}] }' | jq -c '.hits.hits[]._source' > rbac-grants.ndjson
- Snapshot policy repo: git -C /infra/policies rev-parse HEAD > policy-commit.txt && tar czf policies-${AUDIT_RUN_ID}.tgz /infra/policies && sha256sum policies-${AUDIT_RUN_ID}.tgz > policies.sha256
- Build bundle: tar czf evidence-${AUDIT_RUN_ID}.tgz rbac-grants.ndjson policies-${AUDIT_RUN_ID}.tgz findings.md && gpg --armor --sign evidence-${AUDIT_RUN_ID}.tgz

Mapping notes for Dedicated and Private exports:
- Dedicated: support both centralized Redwood export and customer forwarder. Add field export_mode: centralized | forwarder and forwarder_endpoint (masked).
- Private: assume export runs in-customer. Provide a reference exporter (Go binary) that batches and signs NDJSON with the schema_version and tenant signature. Provide instructions for offline transfer if network egress disallowed.

Operational considerations and SLOs for evidence automation:
- Evidence generation time: target < 30 minutes from request to bundle availability for standard audits.
- Tamper-evident: sign bundles and include checksums for every artifact.
- Access controls: only designated evidence owners and compliance team can download; downloads logged.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Canonical actor identity format across SSO providers (okta/google/azure) — proposal: unify to user:<provider>:<id>.
- Break-glass workflow UI vs CLI: do we require a one-click approval in console or a ticket-first approach?
- Telemetry redact rules: default sanitize PII from request body in hosted environment; for Dedicated we may offer opt-in raw payload exports under contract.

Next steps (owners):
- Security: finalize schema and put schema_version enforcement in logging library (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-05).
- Infra: ship reference SIEM forwarder and checkpoint protocol (owner: Alex, due: 2026-03-22).
- Product: update onboarding docs with evidence request flow and break-glass UX (owner: Diego, due: 2026-04-01).

Notes to reviewers: please focus feedback on the required SIEM fields (tenant_id, actor_role) and the proposed default deny + temporary elevation flow. If you have a compliant-specific evidence format requirement, add it to the linked_artifacts and we will add a mapping appendix.

-- End of checklist --
